trendAudit.method: Latest retrievable exact-variant official-store archived observation within July–September 2026 versus verified current selling price. Not a quarter average or completed Q4 comparison.

guide.title: Creatine: why the studied form matters
guide.summary: Monohydrate has an extensive exercise-research base; premium names and smaller portions do not establish superiority.
guide.evidence: Research supports creatine monohydrate for repeated high-intensity work and some resistance-training adaptations.
guide.limitations: Evidence is strongest for particular outcomes and studied protocols. It cannot automatically be transferred to HCl, nitrate or a proprietary blend.
guide.catalogReading: The catalog compares labelled compound mass. Equal grams of different creatine salts are not assumed chemically equivalent; micronization describes processing rather than proven greater efficacy.
guide.safety: Discuss use with a clinician if you have kidney disease or another relevant medical condition. Research protocols are not personalized instructions.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: Absorbed creatine enters circulation and is taken up by tissues, predominantly muscle.
Some is stored as phosphocreatine, which helps rapidly regenerate ATP during intense effort.
Creatine and phosphocreatine gradually form creatinine, which the kidneys excrete.
guide.treatment: A performance aid is not a cure for weakness, fatigue or a neurological disease. Specialist uses require condition-specific evidence and care.
guide.whoMayBenefit: Adults doing repeated high-intensity efforts or resistance training who want an optional performance aid.
guide.routineUse: No universal requirement for a creatine supplement. Healthy bodies make creatine, and it is also obtained from some foods.

whoCanConsider: Adults undertaking structured resistance training or repeated high-intensity efforts who want an optional performance aid.
Vegetarian athletes may be responsive because habitual muscle creatine stores can be lower.
whoShouldReview: Existing kidney disease or unexplained abnormal kidney tests warrants professional review before use.
Athletes in weight-category or weight-sensitive sports should consider potential body-mass increases with their sports professional.
buyingGuide.foodSummary: Meat and seafood contain creatine. The body also makes it from amino acids; food and precursor intake are not a standardized supplement dose.

foods.name: Chicken breast, raw, study samples on storage day 1
foods.detail: Range of day-1 group means from conventional and welfare farm samples, not the range of every chicken product. Raw weight describes the assay, not a recommendation to eat raw meat.
foods.quantityNote: Study-specific composition; not a universal food value or supplement-dose equivalent.

value.targetedUse: Creatine monohydrate supporting a consistent resistance-training or repeated high-intensity exercise programme.
value.reason: Monohydrate has substantial performance evidence for this goal. General fitness alone does not establish the same purchase priority.
worthWhen: The training goal matches the evidence.
A clearly labelled monohydrate product fits the budget and body-mass trade-off.
skipWhen: Paying extra for another chemical form relies on an unsupported superiority claim.
value.scope: Targeted score applies to monohydrate and the stated training goal; it is not a necessity, medical-treatment rating or rating of every creatine form.

dos.title: Match the training goal
dos.detail: Consider the repeated high-intensity or resistance-training context before adding an optional performance product.

dos.title: Compare the same compound
dos.detail: Check that the label identifies creatine monohydrate and a clear amount before comparing pack costs.

donts.title: Don't equate different salts
donts.detail: Equal compound weights do not establish equal creatine content or interchangeable effects.

donts.title: Don't pay for unsupported superiority
donts.detail: Micronized processing or a newer form alone does not establish better outcomes than monohydrate.

intakeGuide.summary: No dietary RDA. Optional monohydrate protocols depend on the training goal, not sessions per week.

targets.label: Creatine monohydrate
targets.notes: Optional maintenance protocol studied with training; loading is not required. Applies to monohydrate, not an assumed equivalent dose of another salt.

notes: No automatic dose increase is assigned for training frequency or experience.

medicalGuide.summary: Condition-specific evidence, separate from sports benefits and purchase priority.

conditions.findings: Creatine is not established treatment for dementia or a cognitive disorder. Cognition signals in other populations cannot establish that indication.
conditions.limits: A performance aid is not a cure for weakness, fatigue or a neurological disease. Specialist uses require condition-specific evidence and care.

conditions.findings: The large NET-PD trial did not demonstrate slower clinical progression and was stopped for futility.
conditions.limits: A performance aid is not a cure for weakness, fatigue or a neurological disease. Specialist uses require condition-specific evidence and care.

pathway.title: Creatine supplies a rechargeable phosphate buffer
pathway.summary: Creatine reaches muscle through the blood. The creatine kinase system transfers phosphate between creatine and ATP as energy demand changes.

steps.label: Oral creatine reaches the intestine
steps.detail: Ingested creatine is absorbed rather than being digested like a whole dietary protein.

steps.label: Circulation carries the absorbed creatine
steps.detail: Blood transports absorbed creatine to target tissues.

steps.label: Transporters bring creatine into muscle
steps.detail: Creatine transporters deliver creatine into cells, adding to the creatine and phosphocreatine pool.

tracks.label: The creatine kinase buffer
tracks.returnLabel: ATP can recharge the creatine pool

steps.label: Creatine receives phosphate from ATP
steps.detail: Creatine kinase uses ATP to form phosphocreatine and ADP.

steps.label: Phosphocreatine holds transferable phosphate
steps.detail: Phosphocreatine provides a rapidly available phosphate reserve within the cell.

steps.label: Phosphate transfer rapidly regenerates ATP
steps.detail: When demand rises, creatine kinase transfers phosphate to ADP, regenerating ATP and leaving creatine.

pathway.caveat: The buffer supports ATP availability during intense effort; it does not replace ongoing energy production or establish treatment benefits for cognitive disorders.
